research.summary: The curated 60-day market-event feed returned no entries as of 2026-04-06, and news/web search are unavailable in this brief, so the only usable evidence is the frozen price/volume snapshot. That snapshot shows a defensive, late-cycle tape: SPY is -3.0% over 30 days and below its 50-day SMA, mega-cap tech is weak (MSFT -9.2% 30d, RSI 30; META -13.2% 30d; GOOGL, AMZN, AVGO all below 50-day), while energy (USO +44% 30d at 52-week highs, XOM +8.4%, CVX +4.7%) and defensives/staples (WMT, COST, JNJ, NEE, LIN) are the clear leadership. Gold has pulled back (-8.3% 30d) and long bonds are flat-to-soft, so the inflation/commodity impulse is concentrated in oil. With a 125-trading-day hold to 2026-10-02 and a 4% max position cap, the evidence favors a broad, diversified allocation tilted toward energy, staples/healthcare, and quality industrials, with reduced mega-cap tech weight and small hedge sleeves.

UNH (-51.7% off high, -43.7% 12-1 momentum) and PG (RSI 20.3) show company-specific deterioration that price data cannot explain without news; a value trap is plausible over 6 months.

opportunities: Energy complex (XOM, CVX, USO) is the only group with strong positive 30d/90d momentum and price above all SMAs; XOM/CVX offer trend with reasonable vol, USO offers the strongest momentum but at 73% vol and RSI 68.
Defensive quality uptrends with low volatility and shallow drawdowns: JNJ, COST, WMT, NEE, LIN all sit above all SMAs, within ~5% of highs, and have outperformed SPY over 30d and 90d.
Mega-cap tech is oversold relative to its own 12-1 momentum (MSFT RSI 30, META RSI 37, GOOGL/NVDA near SMA-200); a mean-reversion bounce is plausible, though trend confirmation is absent.
JPM is the standout financial with positive 30d return, RSI 64, and price above SMA-20 while the broad market is down 3% over 30d.
TLT at 11.6% vol and flat trend is a cheap low-volatility diversifier if equity weakness persists.
risks: Broad market is in a mild downtrend: SPY -3.0% 30d, -3.3% 90d, below SMA-50, with most mega-cap tech (MSFT, META, GOOGL, AVGO, AMZN) below their SMA-200s.
USO's parabolic move (+101% in 90d, 73% annualized vol, RSI 68) is prone to violent reversal; energy exposure is a crowded, extended trade.
Momentum dispersion is extreme: 12-1 momentum ranges from -44% (UNH) to +114% (CAT), so naive momentum screens carry large single-name blowup risk.
Several names are deeply broken (UNH -52% off highs, MSFT -31%, META -27%) and could keep bleeding; catching these knives is a real drawdown risk.
Concentration limits (4% max per name, no leverage) mean the portfolio's fate is driven by group allocation; a tech-led further leg down would hit any growth-tilted book hard.
GLD's 8% 30d pullback shows the classic hedge is not currently offsetting equity weakness, reducing diversification benefit.

forecaster.method_notes: Forecasts are drift-based (momentum/trend-anchored) statistical projections from decision-date (2026-04-06) price history only; the tool returned a 60-trading-day horizon, which is shorter than the brief's 125-day holding period, so intervals understate true horizon uncertainty and expected returns are not scaled to 125 days. Direction is the sign of expected return; 'flat' denotes near-zero drift. Confidence is a subjective 0.45-0.55 band reflecting wide p10-p90 spreads and the absence of news/fundamental inputs. Excess returns are measured against the SPY benchmark forecast (3.52%), not zero. No knowledge of events after the decision date is used.

decision.rationale: With no news feed and a 4% cap forcing a 22+ name book, the only durable edge is the persistent relative strength in energy (XOM/CVX above all SMAs, +34%/+29% 90d), defensive quality (JNJ, COST, WMT, NEE, LIN all within ~5% of highs on low vol), and JPM's relative strength; I hold these at the full 4% and keep the mega-cap tech complex at 4% each rather than zero, since 12-1 momentum (GOOGL 92%, AVGO 95%, NVDA 66%) is intact and the critic's point that the forecaster's 60-day drifts are unscaled and overconfident cuts both ways. I deliberately cap USO at zero despite the strongest momentum: 73% annualized vol, RSI 68, a parabolic +101% 90d move, and a forecast p10 of only -10% make it a momentum position mislabeled as a hedge, and the critic is right that oil does not reliably offset an equity drawdown. GLD and TLT get 4% each as modest ballast (GLD still +62% 12-1 and above SMA-200; TLT at 11.6% vol), and I hold 4% cash because the benchmark itself is below its 50-day SMA with a -3.3% 90d return, so a small uninvested buffer is cheaper than forcing a marginal name.
